Nella RM mammaria per l'estensione di un:
In breast MRI for the extent of a known carcinoma, describe the index lesion (location, size, shape, margins, internal enhancement, curve) and look for other foci in the same breast (multifocality and multicentricity), in the contralateral breast, in the axillary lymph nodes and in the chest wall.

The enhancement curve is measured with a small ROI on the most enhancing part, not on the whole lesion: type I progressive (generally benign), type II plateau, type III with wash-out (the most suspicious). Here the signal rises by about 135% in the first phase after contrast and then falls: type III. Beware of the technique: the first of the five dynamic phases has the same signal as the mask, so it is still pre-contrast.

Completing the reading: in the outer and posterior part of the left breast, toward the axillary tail, small enhancing oval formations with a central hilum (probable intramammary or low axillary lymph nodes) should be described and evaluated with axillary ultrasound.

Orientation: the patient is prone; the viewer shows axial images rotated by 180°, as they are reported, with the patient's right on the left of the screen (the «Rotate» button returns to the original image).

Completing the read: in the outer and posterior part of the left breast, toward the axillary tail, small oval enhancing formations with a central hilum (probably intramammary or low axillary lymph nodes) should be described and evaluated with axillary ultrasound.
